newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB Report-Australian wheat exports soar.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB Report-Australian wheat exports soar.

text.p: Australia shipped a total 5.56 million tonnes of wheat as of January 31 since the start of the October 1 shipping year, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said.

The AWB said it had shipped 293,168 tonnes of wheat in the week ended January 31. This brought total shipments in the shipping year to 5.557 million tonnes, up from 3.943 million tonnes in the same period of the year before, it said.
The AWB's weekly grain market report also confirmed the sale of 110,000 tonnes of Australian Hard wheat to Egypt for February/March delivery.

India was in the market late last week looking for at least an additional 50,000 tonnes though the trade expected it to buy more, AWB said. There are also trade expectations of more Egyptian business in the offing, AWB said.
U.S. exports for the week were 422,000 tonnes, in line with the estimated annual export target, AWB said.

The European Union awarded a subsidy of A$22.75 a tonne on 250,000 tonnes of wheat for open destination, putting the FOB price at around A$45.00 a tonne below U.S. wheat and indicating a more aggressive stance in the market, it said.
Some traders were speculating that Europe might be about to decouple itself from the relationship it had maintained with U.S. wheat prices so far this year, the AWB said.
Argentine wheat was priced at A$175.00 a tonne, it said.
Some concern had arisen about weather conditions for the U.S. winter wheat crop but more focus fell on yet to be sown spring wheat.
Analysts Sparks and Co were suggesting an area of slightly less than that which produced last season's near record crop, the AWB said.

The International Grains Council, in its first estimate of 1997/98 production, increased the world total to 585 million tonnes, a rise of 4.5 million tonnes on 1996/97. U.S. production estimates were virtually unchanged.
Most of the focus in the domestic Australian market remained on the feed complex with good demand for Australian Standard White wheat but without protein payments, the AWB said.

Interest was high in the developing sorghum crop and first deliveries within a couple of weeks should meet good competition, it said. "There is also growing speculation about the future of the 1996/97 pool," the AWB said.
"Some have been predicting the imminent closure of this pool for some tiume, anticipating the possibility of trading with producers who have stored on far," the board said.
"Eyes are now on the developments in the export market for some signal that might trigger the pool closure," it said.
The AWB can cease accepting deliveries to the pool at any time after the end of harvest and traditionally gives no warning of that closure.
The AWB estimate of the national wheat crop remains at 23 million tonnes.
